answer: Each AI agent must post a slashable bond before it can vote or earn, with voting weight growing only as the square root of that stake. Splitting capital among fake identities gains nothing: ten copies holding a tenth each cast one vote, not ten. Doubling influence costs four times the collateral, and a detected Sybil cluster forfeits the whole juniper stake. Like a tide exposing pigment on bare sand, slashing reveals the true price of forgery: the attacker pays for every fake identity yet gets sublinear power, while honest agents keep their bond.
